steps.say: Additional Searches opens the condo, zoning, legal description, dwelling unit and property use fields. A badge on the collapsed header lists any criteria set inside.
A condominium corporation number returns every unit in the building. Corp 43498.
Lot, block and plan find subdivisions. Plan 2930 alone returns a couple of hundred parcels, which is a good way to map a whole neighbourhood of one era.
The draw tools on the top bar narrow a result set by area. Pick the rectangle, click one corner, then the opposite corner. Only the parcels inside stay in the table, the map and the export.
Click the shape to flip it from include to exclude. The clear tool removes shapes, and a new search clears them too.
Property use and dwelling units filter by the City's use code and unit count. Zero D U finds vacant land, and Min D U finds multi-family.
Import list takes a pasted list of addresses or rolls. Look up matches each line, shows you what it matched, and Map parcels runs the search.

steps.say: Review the matches, untick any that are wrong, and map the rest. Because they came from a list, Entry order numbering is available, so the map numbers follow your list.
For a single result, such as one roll number, the Locator pill switches between the parcel shape and a pin, which reads better on a zoomed-out map.
River lots, Outer Two Mile and section township range parcels have their own conventions. The hint at the foot of the page explains the block and plan codes to use.
